acceptance.statement: POST /links creates a link, supports a custom alias and an idempotency key, and rejects invalid input with 400 / 409
GET /{code} answers 302 with the original URL, 404 for unknown codes and 410 for expired links
A token-bucket limiter returns 429 with Retry-After once the burst is exhausted
GET /links/{code}/stats reports an exact click count and /metrics exposes the service counters
Parallel redirects never lose a click: 8 threads x 40 redirects must land as exactly 320
A SIGKILL during operation loses no link and no click counter after restart on the same database
SIGTERM produces a clean shutdown with exit status 0
Redirect latency stays at or below 75 ms at p99
The redirect path sustains at least 200 requests per second
The service starts as `python3 -m linksvc` and prints a machine-readable ready line with its port
GET /links/top?limit=N returns the most-clicked links ordered by clicks (ties broken by creation time), defaults to 10 and rejects a limit outside 1..100 with 400

exports.linksvc.analytics.top_links: top_links(store: LinkStore, limit: int = 10) -> list[LinkStats] ordered by clicks desc, then created_at asc
exports.linksvc.ratelimit.TokenBucketLimiter: TokenBucketLimiter(rate: float, burst: int) with allow(key: str) -> tuple[bool, float] returning (allowed, retry_after_seconds)
exports.linksvc.server.serve: serve(host: str, port: int, db_path: str, rate: float, burst: int) -> int
exports.linksvc.storage.Link: dataclass(code: str, url: str, created_at: float, expires_at: float | None)
exports.linksvc.storage.LinkStats: dataclass(code: str, url: str, clicks: int, created_at: float, expires_at: float | None)
exports.linksvc.storage.LinkStore: LinkStore(db_path: str) with create(url, code=None, ttl_seconds=None, idempotency_key=None) -> Link, get(code) -> Link | None, record_click(code) -> None, stats(code) -> LinkStats | None, count_links() -> int, close() -> None
exports.linksvc.storage.errors: InvalidUrl, InvalidAlias, DuplicateAlias (all subclasses of StorageError)

contracts.summary: Frozen module boundaries. Workers implement these exactly; they may not renegotiate them.

done_when: top_links returns links ordered by clicks descending, ties broken by created_at ascending
an out-of-range or non-integer limit raises InvalidLimit rather than returning a wrong page
the aggregate runs as SQL, not by walking every link in Python

tests: unit tests for ordering, ties, limits and an empty store
